h: Wraxall, Tyntesfield and the Somerset Coast
p: Noah's Ark Zoo Farm sits at Wraxall, a village west of Bristol, and the area around it is rich with things to do. Because the site is spread out, it's worth thinking about the order you'll tackle things in. Starting with the bigger animals while the kids are fresh, then heading for the farm and play areas as legs start to tire, tends to work well. The famous maze on site is a fun challenge too, so make sure you save some energy for getting lost.

Right on the doorstep, Tyntesfield is a spectacular Victorian Gothic house run by the National Trust, surrounded by gardens, woodland and a kitchen garden. It's ideal for a day when the grandparents are along, and the grounds have plenty of space for younger visitors to explore. A short drive towards the coast brings you to Clevedon, where the elegant Victorian pier stretches out into the Severn Estuary, and the seafront has a marine lake and a pleasant promenade.

On the Bristol side, Ashton Court Estate offers huge parkland with deer, woodland and views across the city, and it's free to roam. Clifton Village, close to the suspension bridge, has independent shops, cafes and the Observatory overlooking the Avon Gorge. In the city centre, the harbourside is home to Brunel's SS Great Britain, a fabulous museum ship, and the M Shed museum telling Bristol's story. It makes for a cracking long weekend, with animals one day and city adventures the next.
